texts.value: Transmembrane reductase that may use ascorbate as an electron donor in the cytoplasm and transfer electrons across endoplasmic reticulum membranes to reduce monodehydro-L-ascorbate radical and iron cations Fe(3+) in the lumen of that compartment

reaction.name: monodehydro-L-ascorbate radical(out) + L-ascorbate(in) = monodehydro-L-ascorbate radical(in) + L-ascorbate(out)
Fe(3+)(out) + L-ascorbate(in) = monodehydro-L-ascorbate radical(in) + Fe(2+)(out) + H(+)

texts.value: Optimum pH is 6-7 for the electron donation reaction to monodehydroascorbate reaction (PubMed:23641721). Optimum pH is around 6.5 for re-reduction reaction process of the oxidized heme with ascorbate (PubMed:23641721).

E(0) is +89.5 mV for the high potential heme and +13.1 mV for the low potential heme (PubMed:19734123). E(0) is +109 mV for the high potential heme and +26 mV for the low potential heme (PubMed:23235316).
